subject: geography
title: World Biomes
welcome_lead: From steamy rainforests to icy tundra, our planet has many biomes. Let's tour the world's great ecosystems!
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on world biomes including rainforest, desert and tundra.
final_note: Brilliant! You now know the main world biomes.

concepts.def: Large ecosystem with similar climate and life.
Hot, wet biome with huge biodiversity.
Cold, treeless biome near the poles.
Cold forest biome of conifers in the north.

walkthroughs.body_html: Found near the Equator. Hot all year (~28°C) with heavy rain. Home to half the world's species!
The Sahara and Arabian deserts get under 250mm rain per year. Plants and animals must conserve water.
The tundra has frozen ground (permafrost). The taiga further south has vast pine forests. Both are cold most of the year.

mcqs.q: What is lag time on a storm hydrograph?
options: Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.
Lag time is how long the storm itself lasts.
The time between peak rainfall and peak river discharge — affected by drainage basin shape, land use, soil saturation and vegetation.
El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.

mcqs.q: In a tropical rainforest nutrient cycle, where is most of the nutrient stored?
options: El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.
In the biomass (living plants). Litter is rapidly decomposed by warm humid conditions, and soil is leached — so cycling between biomass and litter dominates.
Most nutrients in a rainforest are stored in the soil — that's why plants grow so well.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.

mcqs.q: What happens during an El Nino event?
options: Trade winds weaken, warm water that normally pools in the western Pacific spreads east, disrupting weather patterns globally — drought in Australia, floods in South America.
El Nino is when the ocean gets colder near Peru.
El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.
Most rainforest nutrients are stored in animals.
